article_content: (CNN) -- FA Cup finalists Portsmouth will not play in next season's Europa League, the English Football Association (FA) confirmed. The financially-stricken side became the first Premier League club to enter administration this year. Chelsea, Portsmouth's final opponents, secured a Champions League spot, which would have guaranteed Portsmouth a Europa League place. However, Portsmouth's administrators revealed a $170m debt, and were told their late UEFA club licence application wouldn't be considered due to financial issues. The FA and Premier League stated: 'The FA and Premier League will not consider any late application for a UEFA Club Licence for the 2010-11 season.' The seventh-place Premier League team, currently Liverpool, will take Portsmouth's Europa League spot. UEFA allowed late applications until May 31, but the FA and Premier League said Portsmouth wouldn't meet UEFA's criteria. Administrator Andrew Andronikou said: 'We've done our part, and it's up to the FA and Premier League to do theirs. It's unfair to fans that they can't support their club in Europe.'

article_content: A new spray-on medication called 'Tempe' is expected to be available in bathroom cabinets as early as next year. Premature ejaculation affects at least one in four men. In trials, men using Tempe lasted five times longer on average, with both men and their partners reporting greater satisfaction. Tempe contains low doses of two anaesthetics. While some users experienced side-effects, Tempe has the potential to be a significant new treatment option.

article_content: Researchers claim that couples who adhere to traditional gender roles in the home have sex more frequently, with an average of five times a month. The study, published in the American Sociological Review, examined 4,500 heterosexual US marriages and found that couples where men participate more in traditionally masculine tasks report higher sexual frequency. Dr Sabino Kornrich, the study's lead author from the Juan March Institute in Madrid, stated that 'our findings suggest the importance of socialised gender roles for sexual frequency in heterosexual marriage.'

article_content: A recent earthquake in Iceland has heightened concerns about a potential large-scale volcanic eruption. The quake, measuring 4.5 in magnitude, has moved around 50 million cubic meters of molten rock towards another volcanic system. Experts warn that this movement could trigger a significant eruption if it interacts with the Askja volcanic system. This development follows a 5.7 magnitude earthquake the previous day, which led to considerations of raising the warning code to red. The seismic activity at Iceland's largest volcano system has sparked worries about another ash cloud like the one caused by the Eyjafjallajokull volcano in 2010. Professor Bob White from the University of Cambridge noted that while it's difficult to predict an eruption, the movement of molten rock is a significant indicator. The Icelandic authorities have lowered the warning code to orange after determining that the seismic activity hadn't resulted in an eruption under the glacier.

article_content: (CNN) -- The chief prosecutor at the International Criminal Court says he has evidence proving Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir is guilty of genocide, although al-Bashir isn't charged with the crime. Omar al-Bashir remains president and has traveled to several countries since the warrant was issued. Luis Moreno-Ocampo told CNN on Wednesday, two days after he appealed to the court to add genocide to al-Bashir's existing arrest warrant. The court issued the warrant in March on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity related to his five-year campaign of violence in western Sudan's Darfur region. 'The evidence shows it is genocide,' Moreno-Ocampo said. The warrant was the first ever issued for a sitting head of state by the world's only permanent war crimes tribunal, based in The Hague, Netherlands. The United Nations estimates that 300,000 people have been killed in the Darfur conflict, and 2.5 million have been forced to flee their homes. Sudan denies the death toll is that high. The violence in Darfur started in 2003 after rebels began an uprising against the Sudanese government.

article_content: Britain's human rights chief, Trevor Phillips, has criticized the interpretation of human rights laws, stating they have 'fallen into disrepute'. article_content: 'Invisible Woman': Methodist minister Sara Cliff has quit her post as councillor for Lincoln East after fierce protests from residents that she lived over 100 miles away from the ward. A Methodist minister who received £23,000 as a councillor for a deprived area while living more than 100 miles away has resigned due to fierce opposition. Reverend Sara Cliff moved to Soham, 119 miles away in Cambridgeshire, after being elected as a Tory councillor for Lincoln East. She attended council sessions in Lincolnshire just 19 times in three years and was paid an average of £1,200 in allowances per session. Critics labelled her the 'Invisible Woman'. Mrs Cliff confirmed her resignation, criticizing the 'unwarranted hostility' that forced her hand.

article_content: Clashes between riot police and opposition protesters in Mozambique's capital, Maputo, have reportedly left hundreds injured and several dead. The main opposition party, Renamo, called for demonstrations on Tuesday due to 'massive fraud' in last week's municipal elections. Protesters were seriously injured fleeing police, who fired tear gas and live ammunition. Renamo president Ossufo Momade urged Mozambicans to take part in a general demonstration, stating, 'This is the beginning of the revolution in Mozambique; stand firm against the oppressive Frelimo regime.' Protests were reported in Chiure, Montepuez, and Nampula, with eyewitnesses describing police brutality. Frelimo was announced as the winner in most municipalities, but Renamo's Venancio Mondlane claimed victory based on 'undisputed evidence.' The Maputo Provincial Electoral Commission reported Frelimo's Rasaque Manhique won 58.78% of votes, while Mondlane secured 33.59%. Renamo accused the government of 'stealing' the elections. A 16-year-old boy was shot dead by police in Chiure, Cabo Delgado province, during celebrations. Human Rights Watch accused the police of 'lethal force' against opposition supporters, stating it was part of a 'coordinated effort to suppress dissent.' The elections are widely seen as rigged, with calls for international action.

article_content: ISLAMABAD - Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan will travel Thursday to neighboring Afghanistan for meetings that officials claim will focus on 'revolutionizing' economic cooperation and matters related to U.S.-backed peace efforts aimed at 'swiftly ending' the Afghan conflict. Khan, who assumed power two years ago, is undertaking his first official visit to Kabul at the invitation of Afghan President Ashraf Ghani amid 'unprecedentedly improved' relations that have long suffered from mutual mistrust and suspicions. Officials say a flurry of high-level visits of top government officials and lawmakers in the run-up to Khan's maiden trip have helped 'dramatically ease' tensions and improve economic coordination. 'The prime minister's visit builds on the sustained engagement between the two countries in recent months for enhancing bilateral cooperation in diverse fields,' said Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman Zahid Hafeez Chaudhri on Wednesday. Chaudhri said Khan and Ghani will hold a one-on-one meeting before leading their respective delegations in formal talks. The visit will help 'cement a stronger and multi-faceted relationship between the two brotherly countries,' the spokesman added. Pakistan's links with the Afghan Taliban insurgent group have been the primary source of political tensions with Afghanistan. The two countries share a nearly 2,600-kilometer-long border, and Islamabad also accuses Kabul of allowing fugitive Pakistani militants to use Afghan border areas to plot cross-border subversive acts. Khan's government insists it does not support any faction in the Afghan war and is working to promote a peaceful Afghanistan to ensure regional connectivity and economic prosperity. Landlocked Afghanistan has for decades relied mostly on Pakistani overland routes and seaports for bilateral and international trade. Mutual tensions, however, have significantly undermined bilateral trade activities in recent years. Last September, Islamabad unveiled a string of what officials described as 'groundbreaking confidence-building measures' to facilitate Afghans visiting Pakistan for medical treatment, education, and business dealings. The steps include long-term business, investment, and student visas for Afghan visitors as opposed to traditional one-time entry visas for a limited number of days. Officials say Pakistan also has operationalized all border terminals in recent weeks to facilitate bilateral and transit trade activities to help Kabul overcome increased economic troubles in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic. Khan's government takes credit for arranging months-long historic negotiations between the Taliban and the United States that produced a 'comprehensive peacebuilding deal' this past February, initiating a 'conditions-based' withdrawal of all American and NATO troops from Afghanistan by May 2021. The insurgents in return pledged to stop attacks on international forces and promised to sever links to terror groups, including the al-Qaida network. The U.S.-Taliban pact also opened in September the first-ever direct peace talks between the insurgent group and representatives of the Afghan government to negotiate a permanent cease-fire. But the so-called intra-Afghan dialogue under way in Qatar has mostly stalled, with each side blaming the other for the delay. President Donald Trump's administration has also acknowledged Islamabad's role in facilitating the Afghan peace process and setting the stage for extracting American troops from the longest U.S. war in history. Afghan presidential spokesman Sediq Sediqqi reiterated Wednesday the 'presence of terrorists hideouts' in Pakistan is a matter of concern for the Afghan government, but he went on to acknowledge Islamabad’s policy on the issue has lately been 'radically changed'. Kabul has long alleged that Taliban leaders and fighters have used sanctuaries on Pakistani soil to sustain and expand insurgent activities on the other side of the border. Pakistan hosts about 3 million Afghan refugees and economic migrants, who have fled 40 years of violence, religious persecution, and poverty in their conflict-torn country. Islamabad says the refugee community serves as a hiding place for the Taliban and has been urging the international community to arrange for an early repatriation of Afghan refugees from Pakistan. Last Saturday, the Pakistani government revealed at a news conference what it said was 'irrefutable evidence' about Indian-sponsored terrorism in Pakistan from Afghanistan. A military spokesman said Indian intelligence operatives were running 'at least 100' camps on Afghan soil to train fugitive Pakistani militants with the help of Afghan collaborators. Both Kabul and New Delhi rejected the allegations as 'fabricated'.
translated_content: اسلام‌آباد - نخست‌وزیر پاکستان، عمران خان، روز پنج‌شنبه به دیدار همسایه افغانستان سفر خواهد کرد تا در مورد تقویت همکاری‌های اقتصادی و مسائل مربوط به تلاش‌های صلح حمایت شده توسط ایالات متحده برای 'پایان سریع' درگیری افغانستان گفتگو کند. خان، که دو سال پیش قدرت را به دست گرفت، اولین دیدار رسمی خود را به کابل به دعوت رئیس جمهور افغانستان، اشرف غنی، در میان روابط 'بی‌سابقه بهبود یافته' انجام می‌دهد که از گذشته از بی‌اعتمادی و سوء ظن رنج می‌برد. مقامات می‌گویند که سلسله دیدارهای سطح بالای مقامات دولتی و قانونگذاران در آستانه سفر خان به کاهش چشمگیر تنش‌ها و بهبود هماهنگی اقتصادی کمک کرده است. 'دیدار نخست‌وزیر بر پایه تعامل پایدار بین دو کشور در ماه‌های اخیر برای تقویت همکاری‌های دو جانبه در زمینه‌های مختلف استوار است'، سخنگوی وزارت امور خارجه پاکستان، زاهد حفیظ چودری، روز چهارشنبه گفت. چودری گفت که خان و غنی قبل از رهبری هیئت‌های مربوطه خود در گفتگوهای رسمی، دیدار و گفتگوی خصوصی خواهند داشت. این دیدار به 'تقویت رابطه قوی‌تر و چند وجهی بین دو کشور برادرانه' کمک خواهد کرد، سخنگو افزود. پیوندهای پاکستان با گروه شورشی طالبان افغانستان منبع اصلی تنش‌های سیاسی با افغانستان بوده است. دو کشور مرزی نزدیک به 2600 کیلومتر دارند و اسلام‌آباد همچنین کابل را به اجازه دادن به شبه‌نظامیان پاکستانی فراری برای استفاده از مناطق مرزی افغانستان برای توطئه اعمال خرابکارانه متهم می‌کند. دولت خان اصرار دارد که از هیچ گروهی در جنگ افغانستان حمایت نمی‌کند و برای ترویج صلح در افغانستان برای تضمین اتصال منطقه‌ای و رونق اقتصادی کار می‌کند. افغانستان محصور در خشداری برای دهه‌ها بیشتر به مسیرهای زمینی و بنادر پاکستان برای تجارت دو جانبه و بین‌المللی وابسته بوده است. تنش‌های متقابل، با این حال، فعالیت‌های تجاری دو جانبه را در سال‌های اخیر به شدت تضعیف کرده است. سپتامبر گذشته، اسلام‌آباد رشته‌ای از آنچه مقامات به عنوان 'اقدامات اعتمادساز پیشگامانه' توصیف کردند را برای تسهیل افغان‌هایی که به پاکستان برای درمان پزشکی، تحصیل و فعالیت‌های تجاری سفر می‌کنند، معرفی کرد. این اقدامات شامل ویزاهای تجاری، سرمایه‌گذاری و دانشجویی بلندمدت برای بازدیدکنندگان افغان به جای ویزاهای یکبار ورود سنتی برای تعداد محدودی از روزها است. مقامات می‌گویند پاکستان همچنین در هفته‌های اخیر تمام پایانه‌های مرزی را برای تسهیل فعالیت‌های تجاری دو جانبه و ترانزیت برای کمک به کابل برای غلبه بر مشکلات اقتصادی افزایش یافته در پی شیوع ویروس کرونا عملیاتی کرده است. دولت خان افتخار می‌کند که مذاکرات تاریخی چند ماهه بین طالبان و ایالات متحده را ترتیب داده است که منجر به 'قرارداد جامع صلح‌سازی' در فوریه گذشته شد و خروج 'شرایط محور' تمام نیروهای آمریکایی و ناتو از افغانستان تا مه 2021 را آغاز کرد. شورشیان در عوض قول دادند که به حملات علیه نیروهای بین‌المللی پایان دهند و وعده دادند که ارتباط خود را با گروه‌های تروریستی از جمله شبکه القاعده قطع کنند. پیمان طالبان و ایالات متحده همچنین در سپتامبر اولین گفتگوهای مستقیم صلح بین گروه شورشی و نمایندگان دولت افغانستان را برای مذاکره درباره آتش‌بس دائمی باز کرد. اما گفتگوی به اصطلاح درون افغان در قطر در حال حاضر بیشتر متوقف شده است و هر دو طرف دیگری را به تأخیر متهم می‌کنند. دولت دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا نیز نقش اسلام‌آباد را در تسهیل روند صلح افغانستان و زمینه‌سازی برای خروج نیروهای آمریکایی از طولانی‌ترین جنگ ایالات متحده در تاریخ تأیید کرده است. سخنگوی ریاست جمهوری افغانستان، صدیق صدیقی، روز چهارشنبه تکرار کرد که 'وجود پناهگاه‌های تروریستی' در پاکستان موضوع نگرانی دولت افغانستان است، اما او همچنین اذعان کرد که سیاست اسلام‌آباد در این مورد اخیراً 'به شدت تغییر کرده است'. کابل مدت‌هاست که ادعا می‌کند رهبران و جنگجویان طالبان از پناهگاه‌های خاک پاکستان برای حفظ و گسترش فعالیت‌های شورشی در طرف دیگر مرز استفاده کرده‌اند. پاکستان حدود 3 میلیون پناهنده و مهاجر اقتصادی افغان را میزبانی می‌کند که از 40 سال خشونت، آزار و اذیت مذهبی و فقر در کشور جنگ‌زده خود فرار کرده‌اند. اسلام‌آباد می‌گوید جامعه پناهندگان به عنوان مکانی برای پنهان شدن طالبان عمل می‌کند و از جامعه بین‌المللی خواسته است تا ترتیب بازگشت زودهنگام پناهندگان افغان از پاکستان را بدهد. شنبه گذشته، دولت پاکستان در یک کنفرانس مطبوعاتی آنچه را که 'شواهد انکارناپذیر' درباره تروریسم حمایت شده توسط هند در پاکستان از افغانستان توصیف کرد، فاش کرد. یک سخنگوی نظامی گفت که اپراتورهای اطلاعاتی هند 'حداقل 100' اردوگاه در خاک افغانستان برای آموزش شبه‌نظامیان پاکستانی فراری با کمک همکاران افغان اداره می‌کنند. هر دو کابل و دهلی‌نو این ادعاها را 'ساخته شده' رد کردند.

article_content: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan is demanding that China completely stop pressuring the country's Muslim minority amid warnings from rights groups that Uighurs in China face extreme restrictions on religious activities and mass detentions in so-called 'secret prisons'. The appeal comes as Pakistan has had traditionally complicated ties with its large neighbor, with many Pakistanis openly supporting the Uighur cause. Pakistan's minister for religious affairs, Noorul Haq Qadri, met Chinese envoy Yao Xing this week to discuss the dire situation of the Uighurs in China's western Xinjiang province, described by many as 'occupied territory'. Human Rights Watch says the forcible detention of 'thousands of Uighurs and other Turkic Muslim minorities' in Xinjiang started in 2017 and has escalated since. article_content: A 'renowned' university law professor says his position as an independent U.N. human rights investigator in Afghanistan was 'terminated' under 'intense' diplomatic pressure from Washington. The United States 'vehemently' denies the charge, saying the human rights situation in Afghanistan has 'significantly improved' to the point that a special monitor is no longer needed. Charif Bassiouni says his job as a U.N. independent expert on human rights in Afghanistan wasn't renewed late last month because of his attempts to 'expose' alleged rights abuses by U.S. forces. Mr. Bassiouni, a professor of law at DePaul University in Chicago, had expected a routine two-year renewal by the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights when his mandate expired last month. But, talking from his Chicago office, Mr. Bassiouni says he was 'explicitly warned' about diplomatic pressure not to extend his Afghan mandate. 'Then I was told, beware, the United States is 'aggressively lobbying' in Geneva not to have the mandate renewed,' he said. The move came days after he submitted a report 'strongly criticizing' Afghan governmental lapses on human rights and abuses by U.S. troops. In his report, he accused U.S. forces of actions 'tantamount to war crimes' at Bagram Air Base and makeshift detention centers. Mr. Bassiouni says he tried to access detention centers but was 'repeatedly denied'. 'I didn't think this was causing the U.S. government much concern,' he added. The U.S. denies Mr. Bassiouni was forced out by U.S. pressure. Kurtis Cooper, a State Department spokesman, says a special human rights monitor isn't necessary. 'The consensus view is that the human rights situation in Afghanistan has 'drastically evolved' to a point that human rights can now be monitored under ordinary procedures,' said Mr. Cooper. Mr. Bassiouni disputes this, saying the human rights situation is still 'precarious'. 'The ordinary human rights issues need an advocate,' he noted. Mr. Cooper wouldn't comment directly on Mr. Bassiouni's allegations of U.S. forces' abuses in Afghanistan.

'سپس به من گفته شد که مواظب باشم، ایالات متحده در ژنو 'به شدت لابی می‌کند' تا ماموریت تمدید نشود،' او گفت. این اقدام چند روز پس از آن صورت گرفت که او گزارشی 'به شدت انتقادی' از کوتاهی‌های دولت افغانستان در زمینه حقوق بشر و سوء استفاده‌های نیروهای آمریکایی ارائه کرد. در گزارش خود، او نیروهای آمریکایی را به اقداماتی 'معادل جنایت جنگی' در پایگاه هوایی بگرام و مراکز بازداشت موقت در اطراف کشور متهم کرد. آقای باسیونی می‌گوید او سعی کرد به مراکز بازداشت دسترسی پیدا کند اما 'به طور مکرر رد شد'. 'من فکر نمی‌کردم که این موضوع برای دولت ایالات متحده نگران‌کننده باشد،' او افزود. ایالات متحده انکار می‌کند که آقای باسیونی به دلیل فشار ایالات متحده مجبور به ترک کار شده است. کورتیس کوپر، سخنگوی وزارت امور خارجه، می‌گوید دیگر نیازی به یک ناظر ویژه حقوق بشر نیست. 'نظر مشترک این است که وضعیت حقوق بشر در افغانستان به حدی 'به طور چشمگیری تغییر کرده' است که حقوق بشر اکنون می‌تواند تحت رویه‌های عادی نظارت شود،' آقای کوپر گفت. آقای باسیونی این نظر را رد می‌کند و می‌گوید وضعیت حقوق بشر هنوز 'بسیار ناپایدار' است. 'مسائل عادی حقوق بشر نیاز به یک مدافع دارد،' او اشاره کرد. آقای کوپر مستقیماً در مورد ادعاهای آقای باسیونی در مورد سوء استفاده‌های نیروهای آمریکایی در افغانستان اظهار نظر نکرد.
